title: Europe's Passports Named World's Most Powerful
paragraphs: A passport lets people travel to other countries. But some passports are more "powerful" than others. With a powerful passport, people can visit many countries without a visa.

Every year, a company called Henley & Partners makes a list of the most powerful passports in the world. It is called the Henley Passport Index. The list shows how many places people can visit without getting a visa first.

In July 2026, Singapore had the most powerful passport. People from Singapore can visit 192 places without a visa. Japan, South Korea and the United Arab Emirates were in second place. People from these countries can visit 188 places.

Many European countries are near the top of the list. Sweden was third, with 187 places. Eleven more European countries shared fourth place, with 186 places. These countries include France, Germany, Italy and Spain. In addition, Austria, Greece, Portugal, Switzerland and Malta shared fifth place, with 185 places. In fact, most of the countries in the top 10 places are in Europe.
Not all passports are so powerful. For example, people from Afghanistan can only visit about two dozen places without a visa. It is at the bottom of the list.
Christian Kaelin, the chairman of Henley & Partners, said that a passport is important for "opportunity, security, and economic participation."
This is the 20th year of the Henley Passport Index. The index uses information from IATA, an international airline group.
